algorithm.Title: Sinus Pain or Congestion - Male (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Male
Definition: Sinusitis assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.

Background.ExpertReviewer: PENDING: Qatar adult, pediatric, obstetric, emergency, specialty, and nursing governance review

FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive. Do not delay for another remote assessment or give leftover antibiotics. Keep the person with you; if consciousness or breathing worsens, follow 999 instructions and begin age-appropriate CPR if unresponsive and not breathing normally. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Are sneezing, itchy or watery eyes, and clear nasal discharge the main symptoms without facial pain, pressure, fever, or thick discharge?
questions.Information: Symptoms dominated by an allergic pattern belong in the Nasal Allergies pathway.

questions.Question: Is there swelling/redness around an eye, eye displacement, double or reduced vision, painful/restricted eye movement, severe frontal headache, neck stiffness, confusion, seizure, focal weakness, reduced consciousness, or a rapidly deteriorating child or adult?
questions.Information: Orbital or intracranial complications and severe systemic illness are uncommon but time-critical and cannot be excluded remotely.

questions.Question: Is the person very unwell, are painkillers not helping or symptoms getting worse, or does the caller have a weakened immune system?
questions.Information: NHS.UK sinusitis guidance recommends urgent clinical review or emergency medical assessment for these features.

questions.Question: Has there been no improvement after 7 days of pharmacy or primary-care treatment or 3 weeks of self-treatment, does sinusitis keep recurring, or is the patient 11 or younger?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends primary-care review for these situations.

questions.Question: Is this a typical, recent case with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance: a pharmacist can provide the same treatments as a primary-care clinician for sinusitis.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency sinus-complication response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive. Do not delay for another remote assessment or give leftover antibiotics. Keep the person with you; if consciousness or breathing worsens, follow 999 instructions and begin age-appropriate CPR if unresponsive and not breathing normally. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: eye swelling or visual change; severe headache, neck stiffness, confusion, seizure, or weakness; reduced consciousness or rapid deterioration.

advice.Title: Urgent sinusitis review
Content: Arrange same-day in-person review through the Qatar route approved by governance, with a lower threshold for a young child, pregnancy, immunocompromise, severe pain, dehydration, or worsening illness. Do not use leftover antibiotics or another person's medicine.
Call Back If: symptoms worsen; fever or eye symptoms develop.

advice.Title: Governed sinusitis follow-up
Content: Arrange in-person review for persistent or recurring symptoms. Pediatric age limits, pregnancy-safe treatment, antibiotic criteria, and exact Qatar route require governance approval.
Call Back If: symptoms worsen; new eye, neurological, or systemic symptom.

advice.Title: Governed supportive sinus care
Content: Rest, avoid smoke and known triggers, and maintain usual fluids if not restricted. Saline products and pain/decongestant medicines require age, pregnancy/breastfeeding, allergy, heart/blood-pressure disease, kidney/liver disease, and current-medicine checks under the approved Qatar pathway; do not advise homemade nasal solutions or antibiotics without approved instructions.
Call Back If: not improving as expected; symptoms worsen; eye swelling, visual change, severe headache, confusion, or neck stiffness.
